understand.concept: The standard output stream std::cout is commonly used to display text and values in a console program. The insertion operator `<<` sends values to the stream. Multiple insertions can be chained, and newline characters or manipulators control formatting.
understand.whyItMatters: This concept helps learners write understandable, correct programs and communicate intent to other developers.
understand.analogy: Think of the concept as a clear instruction or label in a workshop that helps everyone use the equipment correctly.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is a guide only; C++ grammar and execution rules define actual behaviour.
understand.explain:
## Include the stream header
`#include <iostream>` makes standard stream declarations available. Use the qualified name `std::cout`.

## Chain output
Several values can be written in sequence with `<<`. Strings, characters, numbers and many other streamable types can be printed.

## New lines and formatting
Use `\n` to add a newline. Manipulators such as `std::fixed` and `std::setprecision` can format floating-point output when `<iomanip>` is included. Formatting state may persist for later output.
